claims.text: The BMW 1 Series (F70) is the fourth-generation BMW 1 Series (the model code used in reviews of the 2024–2026 small-hatch refresh).
Top Gear’s 2025 review says the Audi A3 Sportback has sharp turn‑in, a pliant/neutral ride and a ‘fluid driving experience.’
Auto Express long‑term testing (Dec 2025) reports the A3 delivers comfort and refinement for daily driving.
Auto Express also notes the A3’s automatic (S tronic) can feel jerky at low speeds, which makes stop‑start city driving less smooth than a conventional automatic.
claims.about: Audi A3 S tronic low‑speed jerkiness

claims.text: Carwow’s A3 coverage states the 7‑speed S tronic is ‘seamless on the move’ but ‘can be a bit jerky at manoeuvring speeds.’
claims.about: Audi A3 S tronic behaviour at low speeds

claims.text: Reliability/technical summaries and fault trackers cite recurring issues with the DQ200/dry‑clutch 7‑speed S‑tronic (clutch judder, mechatronic faults) that produce rough or jerky pulls from standstill on affected A3 examples.
claims.about: DQ200 / S tronic common faults causing jerky shifts

claims.text: Owner and enthusiast threads in Audi owner forums report customer experiences of jerky shifts on 35 TFSI / S‑tronic A3 Sportback models and note software/mechatronic updates sometimes improve but not always eliminate the symptom.
claims.about: Customer reports of A3 gearbox jerking

claims.text: Major EU reviews of the BMW 1 Series (F70) describe it as more driver‑focused and engaging than many rivals, with composed, planted handling but a firmer suspension setup that some reviewers say is less cushioned than the A3 over poor surfaces.
claims.about: BMW 1 Series driving and ride character

claims.text: Overview summaries (Car Expert / other EU reviewers) say the 1 Series’ automatic gearbox generally selects appropriate gears smoothly in normal driving, while reviewers recommend the 1 Series if you prioritise sportier handling over the plushest ride.
claims.about: BMW 1 Series gearbox smoothness and sportier ride
